svg.text: Thirty Seven Events — MCP server: how it works
Claude talks to one MCP server. The server runs five tools against MySQL and asks the human before it changes anything.
Claude Desktop · Claude app · Claude Code
You type plain English; Claude reads the tool descriptions and chooses the right tool.
The AI runs in your Claude account — this project contains no AI and needs no AI key.
Same endpoint, same tools as Claude.
Safest: traffic never leaves your Mac.
Demo: npm run demo (asks you yes / no)
Tests: an MCP client against a test MySQL
All of them call the same /mcp endpoint.
Five tools, published to Claude with descriptions so it knows when to use each one:
Shared service layer — all the business rules live here
Built with Node.js · TypeScript · Express 5 (hosts /mcp only) · Zod · Sequelize 6 · official MCP SDK
Two-step confirmation (enforced by the backend, not just by prompting)
1) Ask WITHOUT a token → nothing is saved; you get a summary + a token
2) Claude shows the summary and asks you
3) You say yes → same call again, EXACTLY the same details + token
4) Token checked (unused, not expired, same details) → saved in one transaction
No login yet: add auth before the
server is reachable by anyone else.
The server needs no AI key.
A tunnel URL changes every run.
